_about.title: Simply Sub catalog API: example requests and responses
_about.purpose: The API contract for milestone M2. Every example is validated against the API's Zod response schemas (core's successBodySchemas and errorBodySchema), and every example of a built endpoint is sent to the Worker in tests, whose answer must match its status, headers and schema (PROJECT-PLAN.md task M2.7). Phase 5 endpoints are held to the error envelope until they're built.
_about.dataDisclaimer: All prices, dates and URLs are illustrative. Never seed the catalog from this file.

conventions.envelope: Success: { data, meta }. Failure: { error: { code, message, details? } }.
conventions.docKeys: Keys starting with '_' are documentation notes and never appear in real responses.
conventions.optionalFields: Optional fields are omitted when empty or unknown. For example, a provider without acceptedNetworks, or without the buyer's region (its group, or GLOBAL) in them, takes cards that are 'unknown', so every card is allowed; a provider without availableIn sells where it has prices, and elsewhere it's unknown whether it sells; and a provider without iconUrl has no logo, so the app shows its first letter.
conventions.ids: Stable slugs: provider 'netflix', plan 'netflix.standard', add-on 'netflix.extra-member', bundle 'bundle.disney-crave-premium', feature 'video.quality'.
conventions.rankKeys: Boolean feature: '<featureId>'. Enum or set value: '<featureId>=<valueId>'. Number tier: '<featureId>=<tierId>'. A plan provides an enum key when its value is at least that value, and a tier key when its number is at least the tier's min (PROJECT-PLAN.md §3.2).
conventions.money: Amounts are decimals in the currency's major unit (18.99 = $18.99). Currencies are ISO 4217. Regions are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 ('GB', never 'UK'), a group priced once for all its members ('EU'), or 'GLOBAL' for one price wherever the provider sells. A free plan has one price with amount 0: it creates no charges and the app shows it as Free (PROJECT-PLAN.md §3.1).
conventions.pricing: 'prices' lists every stored price for every region. When a request includes region and currency, a 'pricing' array is added with one picked price per interval, all from one source region and currency (pickPrice, BLUEPRINT §4.7). 'native: false' means the amount was converted, and the app shows ≈ and the exchange icon. A free price (0) is always native, with no fx. 'taxIncluded: true' means the stored price includes sales tax wherever the buyer is (its price's taxIncluded, with the source page's words), so none is added in Canada or the US (BLUEPRINT §4.8). Whether the item is sold in that region at all is a separate check (availability, BLUEPRINT §4.7). Amounts and monthlyEquivalent are rounded to 2 decimals and fx.rate to 4, from the unrounded conversion.
conventions.monthlyEquivalent: Price per month: year ÷ 12, week × 52 ÷ 12, day × 365 ÷ 12, each divided by intervalCount. Computed from the unrounded amount, then rounded to 2 decimals.
conventions.dates: Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
conventions.caching: GET responses carry an ETag based on the catalog version. Send If-None-Match to get 304 Not Modified. The endpoints that read D1 or KV (providers, plans, bundles, fx, icon) also keep each public answer in Cloudflare's edge cache, keyed by its URL, for its max-age.
conventions.headers: Every API response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://sub.simplely.ca (no other site's page can read the answers), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'. The examples show only the first.
conventions.rateLimits: Per IP address, counted in each Cloudflare location: 60 requests a minute to the API, and 10 a minute to GET /icon. Over a limit: 429 rate_limited with Retry-After: 60 and Cache-Control: no-store, and the message 'Too many requests. Try again in 60 seconds.'
conventions.errors: A path or method no endpoint answers gets 404 not_found, and anything unexpected 500 internal. No error may be cached: Cache-Control: no-store, except GET /icon's 404 for a site without an icon.

_about.appUsage: The web app reads the catalog from static files: https://sub.simplely.ca/data/catalog/index.json (the catalog version and the regions with a file of their own), then its region's https://sub.simplely.ca/data/catalog/<region>.json, or /data/catalog.json for a region without one (the same JSON as GET /catalog?region=). Catalog icons are static files too, at https://sub.simplely.ca/icons/<providerId>.webp. The only Worker endpoints it calls are GET /fx and GET /icon (for custom subscriptions). The other endpoints serve deep links, future features and other API consumers.
_about.exchangeRatesUsed: Every converted price below uses the GET /fx example: 1 USD = 1.3806 CAD and 1 EUR = 1.5060 CAD (ECB rates for 2026-10-21, illustrative).

GET /health._note: catalogVersion, catalogUpdatedAt and counts describe the catalog D1 holds: the seed writes them when the catalog version changes (BLUEPRINT §5.3), so catalogUpdatedAt is the build time of the first deploy with that version. A D1 that hasn't been seeded yet has none of them, and /health returns only status and apiVersion.

GET /catalog.description: The full catalog snapshot: features, categories, providers (with plans, add-ons and every region's prices) and bundles. Served from the static files the build writes, byte for byte: /data/catalog.json, or a region's /data/catalog/<region>.json. The ETag is the catalog version, the same for every region.

query.region: Optional. An ISO 3166-1 region code, a group (EU) or GLOBAL. Keeps only the prices pickPrice can pick for a buyer there, whatever their currency: for each plan, add-on and bundle, the region's own prices, or else its group's (EU for a Swede). An item priced in neither keeps every price, since any of them can be the fallback. Every item stays, and meta.region names the region. The response is the static file /data/catalog/<region>.json, or the group's file for a country without one of its own; a region with neither gets the full snapshot, without meta.region (BLUEPRINT §6.3).

GET /features.description: The feature registry: every feature, its type, its values or tiers (the rankable options), aliases and headline flags, in data/features.yaml order, which lists each group before its features. Served from the static file the build writes, /data/catalog/features.json, byte for byte, so each feature keeps its key order. The ETag is the catalog version. Takes no query parameters: any parameter gets 400 bad_request.

data.name: People included
data._note: A plan that doesn't list it is for one person, so there's no single-person tier.

data.name: Includes another subscription
data._note: Values are provider or plan ids (e.g. proton.pass-plus). A plan that lists plans here is a suite, and inclusion is transitive (BLUEPRINT §4.4): overlap warnings, savings and the optimizer use it. Never shown in ranking UIs.

GET /categories.description: Service categories (what a provider is), feature categories (how the Features page groups features) and spend categories (used for card rewards), in data/categories.yaml order. Served from the static file the build writes, /data/catalog/categories.json, byte for byte. The ETag is the catalog version. Takes no query parameters: any parameter gets 400 bad_request.

GET /providers.description: Search and filter providers. Each result lists the provider's plans that match every filter, cheapest first, with picked prices for the requested region and currency, and bestPlanId is the cheapest. lastVerified is the oldest date of the prices shown, and stale means it's more than 90 days old. matchedKeys are the rank keys from feature and from q that the plan provides. matchedOn says why the provider matched: name, alias:<alias>, plan:<plan id> (only when its name and aliases didn't), category:<id> and feature:<rank key>, filters included. meta.query is the query as read, with the defaults it used; total counts every matching provider. The ETag is D1's catalog version and a hash of the query, the exchange rates' date and the static registry's version, and If-None-Match gets 304.

query.q: Free text, 1 to 100 characters, matched term by term regardless of case, accents and extra spaces, and every term must match ('netflix 4k' is Netflix's 4k plans). A term is the longest run of words that a rank key's, feature's or service category's name or alias contains ('ultra hd'), else one word, and one whose last word looks plural also matches its singular ('vpns'). A term matches provider names and aliases, plan names, service category names, and rank-key names and aliases: a boolean feature's own name, else an enum value's, tier's or set value's ('4k' and 'uhd' mean video.quality=4k). One that names no rank key also matches a feature's own name and aliases ('video quality'), and counts with the highest value or tier each plan provides of it. Relevance, best first, is the best term's: a provider name that starts with it, one that contains it, an alias, a plan name, then a feature or category. Each term picks plans: a category it names brings the plans in it; rank keys it names bring the plans that provide one, when any does, and the plans it names; otherwise a provider matched by name or alias brings every plan, and plan names those plans. The plans every term picks are listed.
query.category: Service category id, e.g. 'vpn'. A plan must be in it: its own categories, else its provider's category (Proton VPN Plus is a VPN, though Proton is a privacy suite), and the provider is found by any of its plans' categories. Another id gets 400.
query.feature: Comma-separated rank keys, at most 10, in one parameter. A plan must provide all of them (PROJECT-PLAN.md §3.2). Example: video.quality=4k,streaming.ad-free. A key that isn't in the registry gets 400.
query.minPrice: Minimum monthly equivalent, in 'currency': the plan's lowest picked price (of 'interval', when given), compared to the cent. Needs region.
query.maxPrice: Maximum monthly equivalent, in 'currency', compared the same way. Needs region, and minPrice above it gets 400.
query.interval: Only plans that offer this interval: day | week | month | year. With a region it's among the picked prices, and bestMonthlyEquivalent counts only that interval.
query.region: Region used to pick prices, e.g. CA. With it, plans not offered there are left out (availability, BLUEPRINT §4.7; an unknown one stays, with its fallback price), each plan gets pricing and bestMonthlyEquivalent, and meta gets fxDate. Without it there are no prices, and minPrice, maxPrice, currency, nativeOnly and the price sorts get 400.
query.currency: Display currency, e.g. CAD: the euro or a currency the ECB publishes a rate for. Defaults to the region's main currency, or USD when the ECB has no rate for it.
query.nativeOnly: true = skip plans whose picked price would be converted. Needs region.
query.sort: relevance (default with q, and needs q) | price_asc (default without q, with a region) | price_desc | name (default without q or region) | features (most rank keys provided by the shown plan). Price sorts use the best plan's bestMonthlyEquivalent and need region. Ties go to the provider name.

GET /providers/:id.description: One provider as written, with all its plans, add-ons and every region's prices. With a region, picked 'pricing' is added after the prices of each plan and add-on that isn't not-offered there (availability, BLUEPRINT §4.7): one not sold there gets none, and an unknown one gets its fallback price. It reads 2 D1 rows: the catalog row and the provider's. The ETag is D1's catalog version and a hash of the id, the query as read and the exchange rates' date, and If-None-Match gets 304. An unknown id gets 404 not_found, with details[].suggestion when an id looks like a typo of it (from the static data/catalog/ids.json, so it reads no more rows).

query.region: Optional, e.g. CA: the region to pick prices for, as on GET /providers. Without it there are no prices, and currency gets 400.
query.currency: Optional, e.g. CAD: the euro or a currency the ECB publishes a rate for. Defaults to the region's main currency, or USD when the ECB has no rate for it. Needs region. Any other parameter gets 400, and a region with no exchange rates at all gets 502, as on GET /providers.

GET /plans/:id.description: One plan as written, with a summary of its provider after its name, providedRankKeys after its features (every rank key of the registry it provides, in registry order, PROJECT-PLAN.md §3.2), its add-ons in place of addOnIds (expanded, in that order, each with its own pricing), and bundleIds last: every bundle that includes it, in any region. Lists that would be empty are left out. It reads the catalog row, its provider's row (which holds the plan and its add-ons) and one index entry per bundle that includes it. Region, currency, the 400s, the 404 and its suggestion work as on GET /providers/:id, and the ETag also hashes the registry's version.

query.region: Optional, e.g. CA, as on GET /providers/:id.
query.currency: Optional, e.g. CAD, as on GET /providers/:id.

GET /bundles.description: Bundles that include any of the given plans, sorted by id. Each is the bundle as written, with includes expanded in place (provider and plan names, the provider's icon, and with a region the plan's own picked price on the bundle's first interval as standalone, left out when the plan has none there or isn't sold there), and the union of its plans' features last. With a region, a bundle not offered there is left out (an unknown one stays, with its fallback price), and pricing and savings come after its prices. savings compares the bundle with buying its plans separately: one entry per interval of the bundle's pricing, when the bundle and every plan are offered in the region and every plan has a picked price for the same interval and intervalCount in the same currency, and the bundle costs less. Any other interval has no entry, and savings is left out when no interval has one. Amounts are rounded to 2 decimals and percent to 1, each from the unrounded values. One D1 batch reads the catalog row, each plan asked for (by primary key), the bundles through bundle_plans' (plan_id) index with their sellers, and the providers of their plans: 11 rows for the example. The ETag is D1's catalog version and a hash of the query as read, the exchange rates' date and the registry's version, and If-None-Match gets 304.

query.plans: Required: 1 to 20 comma-separated plan ids, in one parameter. Returns the bundles that include at least one of them. A malformed id, or one the catalog doesn't have, gets 400, with the plan id it looks like a typo of, if any.
query.region: Optional, e.g. CA, as on GET /providers/:id. Without it there are no prices, standalone prices or savings.
query.currency: Optional, e.g. CAD, as on GET /providers/:id.

GET /fx.description: Daily ECB exchange rates (Frankfurter) in the base currency. The Worker keeps one copy in euros for 12 hours (KV) and rebases it to the requested currency, rounded to 6 significant digits. Fresh rates have an ETag of the base and the ECB's date and a max-age of the time left until they're fetched again (43200 right after a fetch), and If-None-Match gets 304. If Frankfurter is down, the last good rates are returned with meta.stale = true, for 15 minutes and without an ETag. meta.fetchedAt is when Frankfurter answered.

query.base: Required. The user's currency, e.g. CAD: the euro or a currency the ECB publishes a rate for. Any other gets 400 bad_request, listing the ones it can be.

meta._note: 1 CAD = rate × target currency. To convert 5.00 EUR to CAD: 5.00 ÷ 0.6640 = 7.53 (an EUR → CAD rate of 1.5060).

GET /icon.description: Icon proxy for custom subscriptions (a website the user typed). Asks Google's favicon service and DuckDuckGo's (core's iconServices) and returns the best icon they give: the largest square PNG of at least 32 pixels and at most 100 KB, usually 64 to 128 pixels, which the app scales down. Google's wins a tie. Nothing else is ever fetched: not the site, and no redirect except to the services' own hosts. Without a usable icon it answers 404, and the app shows the subscription's first letter, as for a catalog provider without a logo. KV keeps each answer under a SHA-256 of the domain, an icon for 30 days and 'no icon' for a day, and both may be cached as long. Neither the domain nor the URL is logged. Catalog providers don't use it: their icons are static files at /icons/<providerId>.webp.

query.domain: Required. A bare hostname such as localgym.example (no scheme, port or path), read in lower case without a trailing dot; an international name is used in its xn-- form. An IP address, a single label such as localhost, or any other parameter gets 400.

response._note: The real body is the PNG image bytes. X-Icon-Source is google or duckduckgo.
Neither service has a square PNG of at least 32 pixels for the site. The app shows the subscription's first letter.

POST /cal.description: Creates an opt-in live calendar feed. The app uploads a minimal schedule (titles and dates only) and gets an unguessable feed URL to subscribe to in Google, Apple or Proton Calendar. The server stores nothing else.

meta._note: The app stores token and manageKey locally. manageKey is required to update (PUT) or revoke (DELETE) the feed, and is never shown again.

GET /cal/:token.ics.description: The iCalendar feed that calendar apps subscribe to.

response._note: One all-day event per charge for the next 12 months, never repeat rules (BLUEPRINT §11.2): the first two are shown. Each UID is the item id plus the charge date. Amounts are what's charged, here with Ontario's 13% HST (BLUEPRINT §4.8).

The request's body is over its route's size limit.
